the_headline.metric: rows visible to #1818's settlement sync predicate
the_headline.predicate: source='kalshi' AND status <> 'resolved' AND resolution_date < now()
reading: THREE. Against 9,938 open Kalshi rows carrying a future resolution_date, of
which the venue-sampled cohort says ~80% of the settled ones have a close_time
already in the past. The repair exists because this predicate is correct code
reading a wrong column: expiration_time is Kalshi's legal backstop, so a market
that finished last Friday stores a date two weeks out and the sync cannot see it.
This is the number to re-read after deploy + backfill.

the_backstop_signature.query: count rows, count distinct resolution_date, and the biggest single shared-date cluster, over kalshi status='open' rows with a future resolution_date

per event. A shared administrative date at this scale is not a resolution date
at all — it is Kalshi's legal backstop, which is exactly what the column holds.
